literal: Ji said: "Equal death—one ought to die fighting!
idiomatic: Ji said, "We all face death—let it be in battle!

literal: How can one sit and accept imprisonment?
idiomatic: Would you rather sit here and be taken prisoner?"

literal: Jin still used the horses' deaths as his excuse.
idiomatic: Jin still pleaded the epidemic among the horses.

literal: Ji then secretly plotted with Wei Juan and others, and selected horsemen.
idiomatic: Ji secretly conspired with Wei Juan and the rest and picked out cavalry.

literal: When Chang came to attack the stockade, Ji went out to meet him; Chang's horse stumbled and he fell.
idiomatic: Chang attacked the fort; Ji rode out to meet him, and Chang's horse stumbled and threw him.

literal: Ji captured Chang and sent him to the capital, was enfeoffed Duke of Xiping, and replaced Dui in commanding all armies.
idiomatic: Ji seized Chang and sent him to the capital, was made Duke of Xiping, and replaced Qiu Dui as commander of the armies.

literal: He Lian Ding was about to re-enter Chang'an; an edict ordered Ji to garrison Puban to resist him.
idiomatic: As He Lian Ding prepared to retake Chang'an, Ji was ordered to hold Puban against him.

literal: The Song general Dao Yanzhi raided Henan to aid Ding, arraying guards along the south bank as far as Heng Pass.
idiomatic: Song's Dao Yanzhi invaded Henan in Ding's support and lined the south bank with garrisons as far as Heng Pass.

literal: Emperor Taiwu campaigned west against Ding and made Ji Champion General, directing the armies against Yanzhi.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu marched west against Ding and made Ji Champion General to command the attack on Yanzhi.

literal: He then crossed the river, attacked Luoyang, and took it.
idiomatic: He crossed the Yellow River, stormed Luoyang, and took it.

literal: Advancing to attack Wulao, Wulao collapsed.
idiomatic: He pressed Wulao until its defenses gave way.

literal: He also, with Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi, pacified Pingtai, capturing the Song generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and the Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo.
idiomatic: With Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi he pacified Pingtai and took the Song generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Dongjun's administrator Shen Mo.

literal: Then he led the army back to the capital and was advanced to princely rank.
idiomatic: He led the army home and was raised to princely rank.

literal: He died; posthumous name Xiang.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Xiang.

literal: Ji as a general was skilled at soothing troops; when he died, every Song soldier who had surrendered sighed in regret.
idiomatic: Ji knew how to steady his men; at his death not one surrendered Song soldier failed to mourn him.

literal: Yu Yeyan, a man of Dai, was later granted the name Yue.
idiomatic: Yu Yeyan of Dai was later granted the name Yue.

literal: His father and elder brother Hechen for generations managed the imperial herds and were gradually promoted to Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.
idiomatic: His father and elder brother Hechen had long overseen the royal herds and rose to Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.

literal: When Zhaocheng died, the Fu clan made trouble within; amid the crisis he gathered livestock until his wealth rivaled a ruler's.
idiomatic: At Zhaocheng's death, as Former Qin stirred within, he amassed herds in the turmoil until his wealth rivaled a prince's.

literal: Liu Xian plotted rebellion; Emperor Daowu was away on campaign, and Hechen escorted the Empress Dowager Xianming back to Daowu and also supplied his resources.
idiomatic: When Liu Xian rebelled, Hechen brought Empress Dowager Xianming to Daowu on his western tour and furnished supplies.

literal: Hechen was made Chief Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: Hechen was made Chief Palace Attendant.

literal: Hechen divided public and private herds of old and greatly missed the mark; Daowu therefore resented him.
idiomatic: Hechen's sorting of old public and private herds missed the mark, and Daowu came to hate him.

literal: Yue alone was respectful, cautious, and disciplined, skilled in perilous moments, and Daowu praised him.
idiomatic: Yue alone was respectful and steady in crisis; Daowu praised him.

literal: With Wang Jian and others he became a senior minister of the outer court and took part in military and state affairs.
idiomatic: He joined Wang Jian and others as senior ministers of the outer court in military and civil counsel.

literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance.
idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance.

literal: When the army was alarmed at Baixi, the Helan chieftain Fuli Juan, the Getuolin chieftain Niwuni, and the Hexi chieftain Chinugen heard of it and rebelled at Yinguan.
idiomatic: When the army was checked at Baixi, Helan Fuli Juan, Getuolin Niwuni, and Hexi Chinugen rebelled at Yinguan.

literal: The Western Pacification General Yuan Shun of Nan'an attacked them but could not overcome them; an edict summoned Yue.
idiomatic: Nan'an's Western Pacification General Yuan Shun failed to crush them, and Yue was summoned.

literal: He defeated and broke the rebel Hu chieftains of Lishi, Huyan Tie, and Xihe, Zhang Chong, and others.
idiomatic: He broke the Lishi rebel Hu leader Huyan Tie, the Xihe rebel Hu leader Zhang Chong, and others.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Xichang and transferred to the Ye Field Secretariat.
idiomatic: For merit he was made Duke of Xichang and moved to the Ye Field Secretariat.

literal: Yue as a general had stratagem; troops obeyed his wisdom and courage, and his name stood above the generals.
idiomatic: As a commander he was resourceful; men followed his wit and courage, and his name topped the generals.

literal: When the Ye Field Secretariat was abolished, the six commanderies he had governed were made into Xiang Province, and Yue was at once appointed its governor.
idiomatic: When the Ye Field Secretariat was dissolved, his six commanderies became Xiang Province and he was made its governor.

literal: He held the law evenly, and the people praised him.
idiomatic: He applied the law evenly, and the people praised him.

literal: Ye had an old round pond; when the season's fruit first ripened, clerks sent some; Yue would not accept it, saying, "The fruit has not yet been presented to the court—how may I eat first!
idiomatic: Ye had an old round pond; when the first fruit ripened, clerks brought him some. Yue refused: "Fruit not yet sent to the palace—how should I taste it first?

literal: His scruple was such as this.
idiomatic: So scrupulous was he.

literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was made Minister of Works.

literal: Yue's nephew's son Lu had committed a crime; all paternal uncles and brothers were executed, but Yue and his son alone were specially pardoned.
idiomatic: His nephew's son Lu offended; every uncle and brother was put to death, yet Yue and his son alone were spared.

literal: The inspectorate reported that Yue's dress was splendid and his bearing and grace rivaled an emperor's.
idiomatic: Inspectors reported Yue's dress too fine and his bearing princely.

literal: Daowu was unwell and full of suspicion; he was therefore executed.
idiomatic: Daowu, ill and suspicious, had him executed.

literal: All at the time deemed it a wrongful death and mourned him.
idiomatic: All who knew him called it injustice and grieved.

literal: Yue was buried on the western border of Shanyang in Dai.
idiomatic: He was buried west of Shanyang in Dai.

literal: Later, when Emperor Taiwu campaigned against the Helian, he passed the tomb and grave; his face changed in sorrow, and he issued an edict to erect a temple and ordered the people of the whole valley to offer sacrifice in the four seasons.
idiomatic: Later Taiwu, campaigning against the Helian, passed his tomb, grieved, ordered a temple built, and commanded the valley to sacrifice each season.

literal: He sought a descendant fit to serve as commander and found his son Ling.
idiomatic: He sought a descendant to lead the line and found his son Ling.

literal: Following campaigns with merit, he was permitted to inherit the title.
idiomatic: Ling served with merit and was allowed to inherit the title.

literal: Wang Jian, a man of Guangning.
idiomatic: Wang Jian was from Guangning.

literal: His father's aunt was consort to Emperor Pingwen and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.
idiomatic: His grandfather's sister was consort to Emperor Pingwen and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: His grand-uncle Feng, as the emperor's maternal uncle, was greatly honored.
idiomatic: His grand-uncle Feng, the emperor's uncle by marriage, stood in high honor.

literal: Feng's son Zhi married Zhaocheng's daughter and was treated with great intimacy.
idiomatic: Feng's son Zhi married a daughter of Zhaocheng and was held close.

literal: Jian in youth married a princess.
idiomatic: Jian in youth married a princess.

literal: At the founding of the state he was a senior minister of the outer court.
idiomatic: At the state's founding he was a senior minister of the outer court.

literal: With He Ba and twelve others he took turns managing routine affairs and joined in planning.
idiomatic: With He Ba and twelve others he rotated through daily affairs and state counsel.

literal: Emperor Daowu sent an envoy to Murong Chui; Jian's words were lofty and Chui admired him.
idiomatic: Daowu sent him to Murong Chui; Jian spoke boldly and Chui admired him.

literal: On return he was made Left Grand Master.
idiomatic: On his return he was made Left Grand Master.

literal: Jian's elder brother Hui was then a grand master; his sons often did not heed the law, and Jian reported the facts in full—Hui and his sons were executed.
idiomatic: His brother Hui was a grand master; Hui's sons broke the law, and Jian reported them—Hui and his sons were executed.

literal: His blunt uprightness was such as this.
idiomatic: So blunt was his uprightness.

literal: In campaigns against the various states he broke more than twenty tribes.
idiomatic: In campaigns he broke more than twenty tribal states.

literal: He also followed the campaign against Wei Chen and defeated him.
idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Wei Chen and defeated him.

literal: He was made Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.
idiomatic: He was made Grand Chief of the Central Tribes.

literal: Murong Bao was defeated at Canhe; the emperor, pressing the victory, meant to sweep Southern Xia.
idiomatic: Bao was crushed at Canhe; the emperor meant to sweep the south in pursuit.

literal: Thereupon the captives were sifted and those with ability were kept;
idiomatic: Captives with talent were kept;

literal: the rest were to be given clothes and grain and sent home, so that the people of the central provinces might all know grace.
idiomatic: the rest were to be clothed, fed, and sent home so the central lands would know Wei's mercy.

literal: Jian held that Bao had been overthrown here, the state within was empty, and to capture and release them would let the foe breed trouble—it was better to kill them.
idiomatic: Jian argued that Bao's realm was hollow, and mercy would breed enemies—they should be killed.

literal: The emperor said, "If I follow Jian's counsel, it is not the righteousness of punishing crime and comforting the people."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "That would betray the war of punishment and comfort."

literal: The generals all held Jian's counsel right.
idiomatic: The generals sided with Jian.

literal: Jian again insisted, and they were buried alive.
idiomatic: Jian pressed again, and they were buried alive.

literal: The emperor afterward regretted it.
idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted it.

literal: Bing Province having been pacified, the imperial carriage exited Jingxing Pass and halted at Changshan.
idiomatic: Bingzhou pacified, the court passed Jingxing and halted at Changshan.

literal: Every commandery surrendered except Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu, which would not fall.
idiomatic: Every commandery submitted save Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu.

literal: The Prince of Wei, Yi, was sent south against Ye; Jian attacked Xindu and other cities.
idiomatic: Prince of Wei Yi attacked Ye; Jian besieged Xindu and the rest.

literal: Jian and the others besieged for more than sixty days without taking them; many soldiers were wounded.
idiomatic: Sixty days of siege failed; casualties mounted.

literal: The emperor himself came from Zhongshan to Xindu and it surrendered.
idiomatic: The emperor came from Zhongshan to Xindu and it yielded.

literal: The imperial carriage reached Julu and broke Bao's forces at Baixi Stockade, then besieged Zhongshan.
idiomatic: At Julu he broke Bao at Baixi Stockade and besieged Zhongshan.

literal: Bao abandoned the city and fled to Helong; within the city there was no lord, and the generals meant to enter by night and seize the gates in victory.
idiomatic: Bao fled to Helong; the city was headless, and the generals meant to rush the gates by night.

literal: Jian was greedy and without plan, his mind on plunder.
idiomatic: Jian, greedy and planless, thought only of loot.

literal: Fearing the soldiers would plunder wildly and pillage the treasuries, he asked to wait until dawn; the emperor then stopped.
idiomatic: Fearing looting of the treasuries, he begged to wait for dawn; the emperor held the army.

literal: That night, refugees together set up Murong Pulin as lord and closed the gates to hold firm.
idiomatic: That night refugees made Murong Pulin ruler and barred the gates.

literal: The emperor then attacked with his full force, sent men up nest carts overlooking the walls, and summoned the people.
idiomatic: He assaulted in force, sent men up siege towers to call the city in.

literal: All said, "We only fear becoming like the host at Canhe, and so beg a full month of life."
idiomatic: They answered, "We fear the fate of Canhe and beg only to live out the month."

literal: Hearing this, the emperor turned, looked at Jian, and spat in his face.
idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor turned and spat in Jian's face.

literal: Zhongshan was pacified; Jian was enfeoffed Duke of Puyang.
idiomatic: Zhongshan fell; Jian was made Duke of Puyang.

literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Herds, then to Duke of Zhending, with additional posts as Regular Attendant and Governor of Ji and Qing.
idiomatic: He became Grand Master of the Herds, then Duke of Zhending, Regular Attendant, and governor of Ji and Qing.

literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Luo Jie, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Luo Jie was from Dai.

literal: His ancestors for generations led their tribe as Wei's attached subjects.
idiomatic: His line had led their tribe as Wei subjects for generations.

literal: At Liu Xian's rebellion, Jie followed Daowu on his visit to the Helan.
idiomatic: At Liu Xian's revolt Jie followed Daowu to the Helan.

literal: Later he was enfeoffed Marquis of Qushe.
idiomatic: He was later made Marquis of Qushe.

literal: In the early Taiwu reign he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Grand Officer of the Outer Capital, overseeing the thirty-six bureaus.
idiomatic: Early in Taiwu he rose to Palace Attendant and Grand Officer of the Outer Capital over thirty-six bureaus.

literal: At one hundred seven his spirit was undiminished.
idiomatic: At one hundred seven his mind was still clear.

literal: Taiwu for his loyalty and honesty greatly trusted him.
idiomatic: Taiwu trusted him deeply for his loyalty.

literal: Overseeing the inner palace, entering and leaving the sleeping quarters, he was therefore made Director of the Palace Harem.
idiomatic: He oversaw the inner palace, went in and out of the royal bedchamber, and was made Director of the Palace Harem.

literal: At one hundred ten an edict permitted him to retire.
idiomatic: At one hundred ten he was allowed to retire.

literal: Great Ning and the Eastern River were granted as a private estate and separate residence.
idiomatic: Great Ning and Eastern River were granted as his private estate.

literal: A city was also built for him, called Luo Marquis City.
idiomatic: A city was built for him, called Luo Marquis City.

literal: Whenever the court had a great affair, a post horse was sent to inquire of him.
idiomatic: On great affairs of state a courier was sent to ask his counsel.

literal: At one hundred twenty he died; posthumous name Zhen.
idiomatic: At one hundred twenty he died, posthumous name Zhen.

literal: His son Jin followed Taiwu against He Lian Chang, fought fiercely with merit, and rose to Director of the Four Bureaus.
idiomatic: His son Jin campaigned against He Lian Chang with fierce merit and rose to Director of the Four Bureaus.

literal: Following the pacification of Liang Province, for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Daifang and made Grand General of Chang'an Garrison.
idiomatic: After Liangzhou was pacified he was made Duke of Daifang and Grand General of Chang'an Garrison.

literal: When the Rouran invaded the frontier, he was made Grand General of Rouxuan Garrison.
idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the border he was made Grand General of Rouxuan Garrison.

literal: He died; posthumous name Jing, buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died, posthumous name Jing, and was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: His son Gan inherited the title and held the post of Director of the Storehouse Bureau.
idiomatic: His son Gan inherited the title and became Director of the Storehouse Bureau.

literal: He died; his son Yili inherited.
idiomatic: He died; his son Yili inherited.

literal: His son Zhen inherited and was demoted from marquis to duke.
idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited and was reduced from marquis to duke.
